W: I love this farm, and I’m so happy to visit it with you guys again.
M: Really? Look, the goats are running around a big box.
W: Yes, they can get water from the box.
M: I want to see the rabbits too. Do you remember where they are?
W: Yes, they are near the farm gate.
M: Great. I hope we can see them later.

M: Excuse me, do you work with the elephants here?
W: Yes, I do. How can I help you?
M: I heard there is a young elephant here, but I cannot find her. Where is she?
W: She is standing beside the large rock.
M: I can see her now. Why is she moving her ears so often?
W: Moving her ears helps her keep cool in hot weather.
M: That’s interesting. Thank you for your explanation.
W: You’re welcome.

W: Welcome to our rescue dog training centre, and today Rocky will show us part of a rescue dog’s job.
M: Great. What is Rocky looking for among those bags?
W: He is looking for a bag with a special smell.
M: Oh, he is checking all the bags one by one.
W: Yes, his strong nose helps him find the right bag quickly.
M: Who is the man telling Rocky what to do?
W: That is Mr Lee, and he works with the dogs here.
M: I see. We will watch from here and keep quiet.

items.text: (W) I’m Emma, a junior high student. In our class, we have plan cards to help us challenge a new project. Every student can write a useful plan on it, so I write a plan about public speaking. We usually put the cards on the bookshelf so everyone can see it. Ben saw my card and wanted to try my plan too. So every day after lunch, Ben and I practise speaking in a small group. I think this can help us speak better.

Plants are a key part of our natural world. We see them everywhere, so tomorrow our class is going to visit a beautiful garden and learn more about these friends. We are going to find out how they help us in many ways. For example, some plants provide food for us, and others give us oxygen to breathe. Some plants can also be homes for small insects. Without them, the world would be very different. I can't wait to explore their magic tomorrow!

Today I am going to plant a sunflower seed in my garden. First, I am going to place the seed gently into the soil. Then, I will water it every day to keep the soil moist. My mum told me it is a long process. A few days later, a small green stem will rise. Gradually, it will grow big leaves to absorb sunlight. Finally, beautiful yellow flowers will come out. What a wonderful experience it is going to be!

A green plant is like a busy factory. First, the roots will send up water. Then, it will rise through the stem to the leaf. The leaf will turn the water, sunlight, and CO₂ into sugar. Another product will be oxygen for animals and humans to breathe. At night, they also take a rest. They work like us, but also give us so much. Because of their hard work, our natural world is full of life!

Welcome to the beautiful forest, a peaceful home for many animals. Look at the river! Some beavers are working together right now. What are they doing? One beaver is cutting down a small tree with its sharp teeth. Some are swimming quickly in the river, while others are trying to build something across the water. It's a dam! People often call beavers nature's engineers. The natural world is full of surprises!

Animals are our fantastic friends, but many of them are in danger. We are losing different kinds of animals every day. To change this situation, scientists are trying to find new ways to help. They do lots of research and put the results into action. For us, there are also lots of things we can do. We can start by protecting their natural homes and saying no to animal products. Even small changes in our daily lives can make a big difference for them.

Henry is studying pigeons for Bird Week. At first, he thinks they are boring and dirty. He watches them in the park and even feels they are scary. Later, he does some research online and finds that pigeons can recognise themselves. He is surprised, so he goes back to the park and sees a pigeon looking at its reflection in the water. He also learns they can fly long distances without getting lost. Now, Henry enjoys watching them because these birds are truly amazing!
Learning without thinking is of no use.
Ms Chen writes the sentence on the blackboard and says, “Please write this down.”
I write down the first word and stop.
But is it OK to point out the mistake?
Is that polite, in the first lesson?
Questions jump into my mind.
I look up at Ms Chen.
My eyes meet hers.
But then I think about the meaning of the sentence.
I put up my hand.
“Ms Chen, there’s a mistake,” I say.
That sentence is from Confucius, not from Mencius.
You need to think more in your learning.
Speaking up in the first lesson is a problem for Wang Han.

In the first English lesson, Ms Chen writes a sentence on the blackboard and asks us to write it down. I begin to write, but I stop after the first word. Questions jump into my mind. But then I think about the meaning of the sentence. I put up my hand. “Ms Chen, there’s a mistake,” I say. Ms Chen says yes and that is the first lesson for everybody. Learning will be more difficult, so we need to think more in our learning.

In the first English lesson, Ms Chen writes a sentence on the blackboard and asks the students to write it down. Wang Han starts to write, but he soon stops. He finds something wrong with the sentence.
He wants to point out the mistake, but he is not sure. Is it polite to do that in the first lesson? Many questions jump into his mind. He looks up at Ms Chen and feels nervous.
Then Wang Han thinks about the meaning of the sentence. At last, he puts up his hand and says, “Ms Chen, there’s a mistake. That sentence is from Confucius, not from Mencius.”
Ms Chen smiles and says, “Well done, Wang Han.” She says, “In fact, this is my first lesson for all of you.” In junior high school, learning will be more difficult. Students need to think more in their learning.
For Wang Han and his classmates, it is really an important lesson.

Welcome to Students’ Union Radio! The new school year is beginning. What are the new student’s problems? Let’s take a look.
For many years, the biggest problems is: They have more subjects and more homework. They also have many activities. So how can they make good use for their time?
Mia, how do you feel about your first day in junior high tomorrow?
Well, I’m a little nervous.
Don’t worry.
We’ve got something for you!
We want to share some thoughts with you.
Time flies!
Are you ready for your new life?
Primary school is like a small pool.
Dad and Mum can protect your boat from winds.
But junior high is like a river.
You will face new problems.
But sometimes you have to sail your boat by yourself.
Just try your best and work hard.
You will go through storms towards the sea.
One way is to face problems bravely.

Before junior high starts, Mia got a letter from Dad and Mum. Primary school is like a small pool. Mia’s boat is safe there, and her parents can protect her boat from winds. But junior high is like a river. It is wide and the water moves fast. Mia will face new problems. Her parents are still there to help, but sometimes she has to sail her boat by herself. She should try her best and work hard. Then she can go through storms towards the sea.

Before Mia’s first day in junior high, Dad asks her how she feels about her new life. Mia says she is a little nervous. Mum tells her, “Don’t worry.” Then Dad and Mum give her a paper boat latter. They want to share some thoughts with her.
In the letter, they say, “Time flies! You are now in junior high. Are you ready for your new life?” They tell Mia that primary school is like a small pool. Her boat is safe there, and Dad and Mum can protect it from winds.
But junior high is like a river. It is wide, and the water moves fast. Mia will face new problems. Her parents are still there to help, but sometimes she has to sail her boat by herself.
At the end of the letter, they say, “Just try your best and work hard. You will go through storms towards the sea.” Mia reads the letter and feels loved. She is ready for her new journey.
